title: Stoughton town manager contradicts police chief who accused him of tampering with Sandra Birchmore investigation
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Stoughton Town Manager Thomas Calter denies allegations of tampering with the Sandra Birchmore investigation.
Police Chief Donna McNamara accuses Calter of harassment, discrimination, and pressuring her to resign.
Calter and McNamara are on leave; Calter disputes discrimination claims and plans to clear his name.

title: Nearly 30 people arrested after investigation into drug trafficking in Western Mass.
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: Twenty-eight people were arrested in Chicopee, Holyoke, and Springfield during a drug trafficking investigation called 'Operation Pinky Promise.'
Officials seized over 12 firearms, more than one kilogram of cocaine, hundreds of fentanyl pills, and heroin in the operation.
The FBI’s Western Massachusetts Gang Task Force led the months-long investigation, using surveillance, confidential sources, and wiretaps.

title: Patriots stock watch 2.0: Who’s rising and falling ahead of preseason opener?
author: Khari A. Thompson
bullets: Romeo Doubs and DeMario Douglas show strong play during Patriots' joint practice, boosting their preseason standing.
Drake Maye sharp against Colts, with strong connections to receivers despite one interception during practice.
Reserve cornerbacks struggle in absence of Christian Gonzalez and Carlton Davis, allowing 11 straight completions.

title: The best waterfront hotel in America is in Massachusetts, according to USA Today readers
author: Kristi Palma
bullets: Chatham Bars Inn in Chatham, Massachusetts, ranked No. 1 in USA Today's 2026 10Best Readers' Choice Awards.
The Inn features a private beach, ocean views, cottages, and multiple dining options on its 25-acre property.
Madison Beach Hotel in Connecticut also made the list, ranking No. 4 among the best waterfront hotels in the U.S.

title: Are millionaires really leaving Massachusetts? We don’t know yet.
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: Massachusetts implemented a 4% surtax on income above $1 million in 2023, raising $3.4 billion last fiscal year.
IRS migration data for 2023 showed a net loss of 28,000 people from Massachusetts, but it lacks specific income-level details.
Speculation continues on millionaire migration; differing narratives emerge from available data about domestic and international movement.

title: 7 things to do during a rainy day on the Cape
author: Kristi Palma
bullets: Visit the family-friendly Chatham Shark Center to learn about sharks with interactive exhibits and educational programs.
Enjoy indoor water activities at Fins Up! Waterpark in Hyannis without needing a resort stay, with day passes available.
Explore Cape museums and historic homes including the John F. Kennedy Hyannis Museum and the 1675 Hoxie House in Sandwich.

title: Visit to Boston made Boca Raton resident feel miserable about living in Boca Raton
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Boca Raton resident Ian Pinto felt inspired to move after a Boston visit showed him city's appeal.
Pinto highlighted Boston's walkability, public transport, and affordable pricing compared to Boca Raton.
He praised Boston's welcoming community and plans to travel more, considering a future move.

title: Motorcyclist killed in crash with pickup truck in Raynham
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Jason Marshall, 31, of Taunton, died in a motorcycle accident with a pickup truck in Raynham.
The crash occurred at the intersection of Route 138 and Elm Street shortly before 8 p.m. Tuesday.
State Police Detective Unit and Raynham police are investigating the crash involving a 2015 Chevy Silverado.

title: Lindsay Clancy sobs in court as medical examiner testifies about children’s autopsies
author: Abby Patkin
bullets: Lindsay Clancy sobbed in court during medical examiner testimony about her children's autopsies, leading to a recess.
Dr. Barbara Olson testified that Cora and Dawson Clancy died of asphyxia, consistent with ligature strangulation injuries.
Dr. Renee Stonebridge found oxygen deprivation injuries in the Clancy children, consistent with asphyxial incidents.

title: Q&A: Boston’s nightlife czar says the city is just getting started
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: Corean Reynolds, appointed in 2023, aims to expand Boston's nightlife and 24-hour economy.
Boston piloted social districts allowing outdoor drinking, resulting in increased business revenues with no complaints.
Challenges include improving legislation, extending transportation, and issuing more liquor licenses for vibrant nightlife.
